items.t: Said employers face a rising unemployment tax rate and that action is needed to ease the tax burden on employers during the economic crisis.
items.q: By next year, the unemployment tax rate is expected to rise to the highest bracket, requiring employers to pay more at a time when many will likely still be getting back on their feet. We need to take action to ease the tax burden on employers during this economic crisis.

items.t: Said the state is giving towns a new tool to redevelop, based on a program with proven results.
items.q: Not only are we giving towns a new tool to help them smartly redevelop, but we are basing it on a highly successful program that has proven results,

items.t: Defended his redistricting legislation in an op-ed, saying that using statewide elections as the rubric for how districts are drawn was an "anti-gerrymandering test."
items.q: Greenwald wrote an op-ed in which he defended his legislation, claiming that using statewide elections as the rubric for how districts are drawn was actually an “anti-gerrymandering test.

items.t: Said the Next New Jersey Manufacturing Program shows the state is open for business and is about building a New Jersey that prioritizes good paying jobs and long-term economic growth.
items.q: “The Next New Jersey Manufacturing Program makes clear that our state is open for business and we are ready to compete for the industries and innovation that will define the future,” said Assembly Majority Leader Greenwald. “This is about building a stronger, smarter New Jersey that prioritizes good paying jobs and long-term economic growth.”

record.office: Majority Leader, New Jersey General Assembly
record.t: Sponsored legislation that would require state-level districts to reflect the partisan leanings of the state in statewide elections for president, governor, and U.S. Senate.
record.q: New Jersey Assembly Majority Leader Louis Greenwald (D) sponsored a piece of legislation that would require state-level districts to reflect the partisan leanings of the state in statewide elections for president, governor, and U.S. Senate.

record.office: Majority Leader, New Jersey General Assembly
record.t: Was a primary sponsor of A5687/S4407.
record.q: The primary sponsors of A5687/S4407 are Senators Michael Testa and Linda Greenstein, and Assemblymembers Louis Greenwald, Antwan McClellan, and Verlina Reynolds-Jackson.

record.t: Was a sponsor of the New Jersey bill to join the federal ABLE Act program.
record.q: The New Jersey bill was sponsored by Senators Stephen Sweeney and Dawn Marie Addiego and Assembly members Pamela Lampitt, Louis Greenwald, Valerie Vainieri Huttle, Daniel Benson and Vincent Mazzeo.

record.t: Was a sponsor, with Senator Madden, of a bill to ease unemployment tax rate increases on employers.
record.q: We commend the Governor, Senate President Sweeney, Assembly Speaker Coughlin, and the sponsors – Senator Madden and Assembly Majority Leader Greenwald - for their support in making sure our employers do not experience “sticker shock”
